followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the shared April 2022 trucker-protest parent with two facility phases. The obstruction at international commercial lanes is distinct from Texas’s continuing vehicle-inspection policy. Retain northbound and southbound commercial access at Pharr and Ysleta. Personal vehicles and pedestrians at Ysleta remain outside its phase; uncertain exceptional commercial passage is not erased. Retain Pharr’s April 11–13 two-day calendar difference and Ysleta’s April 11 to April 12–13 one-to-two-day range. Protest removal late Tuesday and operating return Wednesday bound the latter without establishing first-truck time. The facility durations are not summed. Retain Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests for truckers’ objections to added inspections and delays. Texas’s migration/security explanations belong to the separate state policy, not the protesters’ rationale. Texas Tribune supplies occurrence with attributed Ysleta details; FreightWaves and KSAT quote CBP for returns. Shared CBP origins are not counted as independent operational confirmations. KSAT’s driver-trip remarks cannot be reassigned from their Progreso context. Retain separate unlocated Pharr–Reynosa and Ysleta–Zaragoza commercial-lane text, null coordinates and facility-specific intervals. Anzalduas, Progreso and other inspection queues are not added to these phases.
